fields.label: Statement
fields.value: An asexual mutant female in a sexual population with equal sex ratio produces twice as many grandchildren as a sexual female, so sex needs a compensating advantage of up to twofold to persist.

fields.label: Notation
fields.value: with equal fecundity and a 1:1 sex ratio, the odds of asexual to sexual females double each generation: \frac{q_{t+1}}{1-q_{t+1}} = 2\frac{q_t}{1-q_t}

fields.label: Source as written
fields.value: John Maynard Smith (1978) The Evolution of Sex

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: Cursor agent (Claude Opus 5.5) extracting key claims from source papers

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: anisogamy with males contributing no resources, equal fecundity and viability of sexual and asexual females, a 1:1 sex ratio

fields.label: Formal status in the nanopub
fields.value: proved as a population-dynamic identity under these assumptions. Its biological force depends on how often those assumptions hold.

fields.label: Notation
fields.value: with equal fecundity and a 1:1 sex ratio, the odds of asexual to sexual females double each generation: \frac{q_{t+1}}{1-q_{t+1}} = 2\frac{q_t}{1-q_t}

fields.label: Proposed test
fields.value: In a species with coexisting sexual and asexual lineages, measure relative per-capita growth of asexual versus sexual females in a common environment and compare it with the predicted factor of 2.
